question.prompt: If \(\theta\) is an acute angle and \(\sin2\theta=a,\) then \(\sin\theta+\cos\theta\) equals

solutions.explanation:
The identity \(\sin2\theta=2\sin\theta\cos\theta\) gives a product of sine and cosine. Squaring the requested sum reveals exactly that product:
\[
\begin{aligned}
(\sin\theta+\cos\theta)^2
&=\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta
  +2\sin\theta\cos\theta\\
&=1+\sin2\theta\\
&=1+a.
\end{aligned}
\]
Because \(\theta\) is acute, both \(\sin\theta\) and \(\cos\theta\) are positive. Their sum must therefore be the positive square root:
\[
\sin\theta+\cos\theta=\boxed{\sqrt{a+1}}.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
solutions.title: Reveal the double-angle product
